clue.text: Make great effort to draw

definitions.meaning: to draw liquid off through a sieve or filter, as tea is drawn from the leaves

explanation.surface: Someone sweating over a sketch, trying hard to draw.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb covers both senses: exerting yourself to the limit, and passing liquid through a sieve to draw it off.

clue.text: Beam, being in better shape

definitions.meaning: in carpentry a short beam framing an opening in a floor or roof

explanation.surface: Someone beaming with pride at having got fitter.
explanation.definitionFit: A builder's term for a framing beam, and the comparative of an adjective meaning slim and neat.

clue.text: Pain suffered by bachelors

indicators.note: the word is carried within the letters of bachelors, as if they put up with it

explanation.surface: Unmarried men endure some hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffered by' signals that the answer is carried inside 'bachelors': bACHElors.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull continuous pain is the standard synonym.

clue.text: Citizen, one working in former British colony

indicators.note: the pieces for one and working sit inside the old colony's name

parts.note: Natal was a British colony in southern Africa, now part of KwaZulu-Natal
I is the Roman numeral for one
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: A citizen employed in an old outpost of the British Empire.
explanation.walkthrough: Natal, a former colony in southern Africa, is split open by the 'in' signal; 'working' as a sense of 'on' is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen or subject of a particular country.

clue.text: See Geoff, after deleting first of -e-mails, close down computer?

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: taking away a letter from the name before it is attached

parts.note: the name taken as written

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the e-mails is used

explanation.surface: Telling Geoff to stop reading his e-mails and shut his computer down.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as advice to Geoff; 'See' is really the old exclamation lo, and the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Logging off ends a session on a computer, a way of shutting it down; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: What one's left, say, in funny clay container

indicators.note: the shuffled clay holds the abbreviation for say inside it
a funny arrangement of the letters of clay

parts.note: EG, for example, is the abbreviation meaning say

explanation.surface: A bequest consisting of an odd clay pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' signals the anagram of clay and 'container' says that anagram holds the abbreviation; 'What one's left' reads as a question but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bequest is the thing a person leaves to someone in a will.

clue.text: Bird, stray one carried in by a soldier

indicators.note: the pieces for stray and one are held inside the bird

parts.note: a gull is a seabird
to err is to stray from the right path
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A soldier carrying an injured stray bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried in by' puts the stray-plus-one pair inside the seabird; the clue's final word is the definition, not part of the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An irregular fighter in a small independent band is a kind of soldier.

clue.text: Large portion of dessert ceases to be enough for gourmets

indicators.note: most of the dessert's name is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a fool is a cold fruit and cream pudding
dies means stops living, ceases to be

explanation.surface: A big helping of pudding no longer satisfies food lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large portion of' trims FOOL, a British fruit-and-cream pudding, to FOO; 'enough for' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name people with a keen interest in fine eating.

clue.text: Wealthy speculator going round European government building

indicators.note: the word for wealthy surrounds the abbreviation for European

parts.note: rich means wealthy
a stag buys new shares hoping to sell them quickly at a profit

explanation.surface: A rich investor circling a building in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Berlin seat of the German parliament is a famous government building.

clue.text: Thoughts about France's voting practices, after leader's ousted

parts.note: re means about or concerning
F is the international abbreviation for France

indicators.note: the voting word loses its first letter

parts.note: elections are where voting takes place

explanation.surface: Musings on how the French vote after their president is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after leader's ousted' strips the opening letter from the voting word, not from the whole clue; 'France's' gives the country code.
explanation.definitionFit: Careful considerations or musings are synonyms of thoughts.

clue.text: Backward dunce given fairly poor grade for poem

indicators.note: the word for dunce is turned to read from the right

parts.note: a dope is a stupid person
E is a low mark in a school grading scale

explanation.surface: A slow pupil gets a low mark for a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' turns DOPE into EPOD; 'Backward' also suits the dunce in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric piece in the style of Horace, an ode with a follow-on part, is a type of poem.

clue.text: Hero singles out an attractive country lass

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A hero picks a pretty girl from the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges HEROSINGLES into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stock description of a fresh-faced, fair-complexioned girl from the English countryside.

clue.text: Musical notes

parts.note: fa is the fourth note of the sol-fa scale
me, or mi, is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A pair of words about music.
explanation.walkthrough: One word 'notes' gives two sol-fa notes side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The stage show and film about a New York performing arts school is a well-known musical.

clue.text: Worrying about…

definitions.meaning: a preposition meaning on the subject of

explanation.surface: Anxious about something, with the ellipsis linking to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: One word is both an adjective for something troubling and a preposition meaning regarding.

clue.text: … old Italian recusant undergoing conversion

indicators.note: the letters are converted into a different order, as a religious recusant might be converted

explanation.surface: A Catholic refusing the established church is converted, continuing the worry of the previous clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undergoing conversion' rearranges RECUSANT; a recusant was a Catholic who refused Anglican services, so conversion suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient people of Etruria in central Italy were early Italians.

clue.text: Spend money getting round of drinks after climbing mountains

indicators.note: the round of drinks comes after the mountains
in a down clue the mountains are read upwards

parts.note: the Alps are a European mountain range
in British and Australian slang a shout is a turn to buy drinks for the group

explanation.surface: Buying a round after a mountaineering trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns ALPS upwards into SPLA.
explanation.definitionFit: To splash out is an idiom for spending freely.

clue.text: Dog fails to finish milky drink

indicators.note: the dog's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Lassie is the famous collie of films and TV

explanation.surface: A dog leaves its milk unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails to finish' drops the final E of LASSIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A yogurt-based Indian drink is a milky drink.

clue.text: Drivers needing less than a minute to cross high hill

indicators.note: the shortened word spans the hill, holding it inside
the word for a minute is cut short by one letter

parts.note: a moment is a minute, a very short time
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Drivers in a hurry to get over a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than' trims the last letter of the word for a minute; 'to cross' makes that trimmed word straddle the hill, a Dartmoor-style tor.
explanation.definitionFit: Motormen are drivers of trams or trains.

clue.text: Extract from Malory Towers about part of Austria

indicators.note: the extracted letters are turned round to read backwards
a run of letters is taken from within the title

explanation.surface: A passage from Enid Blyton's school story concerning an Austrian region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extract from' picks LORYT from maLORY Towers; 'about' reverses it. Malory Towers is a series of British girls' boarding-school novels.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alpine region around Innsbruck is a state of Austria.

clue.text: Rebuke for taking part in endless merrymaking

indicators.note: the word for for goes inside the shortened revelry
the merrymaking word loses its last letter

parts.note: revel means merrymaking, a lively celebration
pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: Telling someone off for joining in the festivities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' clips the merrymaking word and 'taking part in' puts the word for 'for' inside it; 'for' looks like a link but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprove is to scold or reprimand, a synonym of rebuke.

clue.text: Just like a lady, to want to tour part of Middle East

indicators.note: the word for want travels round the Gulf state

parts.note: to wish is to want
Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A ladylike wish to travel in the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tour' has the word for want travelling round the Gulf state; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Womanish means having qualities thought typical of women, here suited to a lady.

clue.text: Development of a region in bygone era

indicators.note: the letters of a region are developed into a new form

explanation.surface: A region was developed long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Development of' rearranges AREGION.
explanation.definitionFit: The period after the Bronze Age when iron tools spread is a prehistoric era.

clue.text: Unknown number on shop floor

indicators.note: in a down clue the unknown sits below, on top of nothing but after the shop

parts.note: a store is a shop
y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: An unknown number of goods on the shop floor.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places Y after STORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A storey is a level of a building, one floor.

clue.text: Hostility in work place

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
a position is a place

explanation.surface: Antagonism in the workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposition means resistance or antagonism, a form of hostility.

clue.text: Magistrate suppresses word of hesitation for a start

indicators.note: the magistrate holds the hesitation word down inside

parts.note: JP, a Justice of the Peace, is a lay magistrate
um is said when hesitating

explanation.surface: A magistrate stops someone hesitating at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppresses' means the magistrate's initials hold the hesitation inside; 'for a start' looks like 'to begin with' but 'start' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden start of surprise is a jump.

clue.text: Short break in Oz is fine in early part of summer month

indicators.note: the first letter of summer is taken
the word for fine goes inside the short month

parts.note: OK means fine

explanation.surface: A holiday in Australia sounds lovely in early summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'early part of' takes only the initial letter of summer; the rest of the clue builds the month abbreviation with fine inside, 'in' doing double duty only in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang for a tea break or cigarette break is a short rest.

clue.text: Where French boy is shielded by soldiers dressing

indicators.note: the French word and boy are protected inside the soldiers

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British army corps
ou is French for where
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A French lad is protected by soldiers while they dress his wound.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is a British army engineering corps. 'dressing' looks like a wound dressing; it is a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Remoulade is a mayonnaise-based French sauce, a salad dressing.

clue.text: Good way in for the aristocracy

parts.note: an entry is a way in, an entrance

explanation.surface: A fine path into high society.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are the landed upper class, the people of high birth.

clue.text: Young person workin' as salesman suffers setback

indicators.note: the letters are turned to run the other way

parts.note: repping means working as a sales rep; with the dropped g of workin' it loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A youngster working as a salesman has a bad time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffers setback' reverses REPPIN, a clipped form of repping copying the apostrophe of 'workin''.
explanation.definitionFit: Nipper is informal British for a small child.
